title: Neue Haas Grotesk / Uppercase specimen
slide_intent: Choose letterforms in relation to the identity’s geometry and meaning because type gives words both a visual structure and an institutional voice.
strategic_value: Bold uppercase letters can connect Whitney’s angular W with a direct, architectural tone.
demonstration: A compact alphabet uses heavy uppercase sans-serif letters, with selected letters shown in gray among the black forms.
practical_value: Compare the angular and curved letterforms with the W, and preserve the essay’s distinction between headline/name treatment and the type family’s wider capabilities.

content_islands.name: Alphabet
content_islands.spec: Pack the uppercase alphabet into stacked rows on white; retain the gray highlights and cropped final row at the image boundary.

reference_purposes.Intent: The adjacent essay links uppercase geometry to the W and explains that capitals make Whitney read as an institution rather than a person’s first name.
reference_purposes.Expression: The specimen shows the heavy uppercase character of Neue Haas Grotesk.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The essay specifies Neue Haas Grotesk for Whitney and uppercase in one selected weight for the word, accompanying headings, titles and names; it does not extend that restriction to all body text.

ingredient.name: Uppercase Neue Haas Grotesk
ingredient.role: Give the institution’s name and headings an angular, architectural voice.
ingredient.application: Set Whitney in Neue Haas Grotesk; the essay specifies uppercase in one selected weight for the name, accompanying headings, titles and names.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2013 rationale. The stated all-caps treatment does not prohibit lowercase throughout the wider type family or all body text.
